issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template repository provides a method named clearInventory() instead. This method-name/signature mismatch is structural: students following the problem UML or the solution example will look for emptyStock() and may be unable to compile or will be confused when integrating their SealSaloon implementation with the provided Stock template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Rename the template's clearInventory() method to emptyStock(), or update the problem statement and solution to reference clearInventory() instead. Preferably change the template method to public void emptyStock() to match the UML and the solution implementation.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template repository provides the same functionality under a different name, clearInventory(). This naming divergence for the same conceptual operation (clearing/emptying the stock) can confuse students when mapping requirements to the starter code and when following the UML/specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (or vice versa update the problem/spec and solution consistently). Aligning the method name across problem statement, template, and solution will remove the cognitive mapping burden for students.
